9: // Found is an error that indicates that a value was not found. It
10: // may be used by low-level packages to signal to higher-level
11: // packages that a value was not found.
12: //
13: // It exists to avoid using errors.New("not found") in multiple
14: // packages to mean the same thing.
15: //
16: // Found should not be used directly. Instead it should be wrapped
17: // or joined using errors.Join or fmt.Errorf, etc.
18: //
19: // Errors wrapping Found should provide additional context, e.g.
20: // fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", not.Found, key)
21: //
22: //lint:ignore ST1012 This is a sentinel error intended to be read like not.Found.
23: var Found = errors.New("not found")

25: // Available is an error that indicates that a value is not available.
26: //
27: //lint:ignore ST1012 This is a sentinel error intended to be read like not.Available.
28: var Available = errors.New("not available")
